articles.title: MillerKnoll, Inc. Q1 2027 Earnings Call Summary
articles.summary: Moby summary of MillerKnoll, Inc.'s Q1 2027 earnings call
articles.body:
Our analysts just identified a stock with the potential to be the next Nvidia. Tell us how you invest and we'll show you why it's our #1 pick. Tap here.

Management attributed the 3.4% revenue decline to softer-than-anticipated demand in North America Contract and Global Retail, partially offset by strong international order growth.

Performance in North America Contract was impacted by a difficult year-over-year comparison due to a $55 million to $60 million order pull-forward in the prior year related to tariff pricing actions.

The company is executing a three-pillar strategy focused on elevating operational discipline, maintaining rigorous cost management, and sharpening capital allocation to support debt reduction.

Management noted that while overall North America demand was soft, internal indicators like project funnel additions and awarded contracts remain constructive, suggesting a timing issue rather than a structural slowdown.

In Global Retail, the company is pivoting toward smaller-format Herman Miller stores to optimize capital efficiency while leveraging direct mail to counter rising digital advertising costs.

International Contract growth is being driven by new product traction, specifically the Concert line by Knoll, which is helping the company penetrate the European private office category.

The full-year sales guidance was lowered to $3.88 billion to $4.03 billion to reflect Q1 softness, though management maintained the EPS range based on expected cost-saving realizations.

Guidance includes an estimated $0.07 per share headwind from recent U.S.-Canada tariff actions, which the company is mitigating through dual-sourcing and inventory pre-stocking.

Management expects price-cost dynamics to become a slight headwind of 20 to 30 basis points in Q2 as inflationary pressures on steel and diesel ramp up.

The retail strategy assumes the opening of 14 to 18 new stores in fiscal 2027, with a focus on stores reaching profitability within their second year of operation.

Capital allocation priorities for the remainder of the year emphasize debt reduction and maintaining the dividend while preserving capacity for high-return growth investments.

Operational Adjustments and Risk Factors

A $16.5 million refund related to previously expensed IEPA tariffs provided a $0.11 per share net benefit, helping to offset volume deleverage in the quarter.

The company implemented a workforce reduction and reorganization within the Holly Hunt brand to right-size its corporate footprint and improve segment profitability.

Manufacturing footprint optimization continues with the closure of a third plant in West Michigan to reduce fixed overhead and improve long-term margins.

Management flagged inventory challenges in the outdoor retail category due to PFAS regulations, though they noted these issues were largely resolved by the end of the quarter.

articles.title: Is Your Savings Turning 16 This Year? How Much Money You've Made
articles.summary: We ran the numbers: what happens when you withdraw $500 yearly from a high-yield savings account for 16 years? The results will surprise you.
articles.body:
Your savings account isn't going to get its learner's permit this year, but if it's turning 16, it should have earned something to celebrate. Maybe it did. Maybe it didn't.

MoneyLion ran the numbers on this scenario: what if you'd opened a high-yield savings account with $500, $1,000, $5,000 or $10,000, then withdrew $500 every single year for sixteen straight years?

The verdict? For most of those accounts, the story doesn't end well. Here's what actually happened.

According to Achim von Bodman, a senior tax manager at Watter CPA , using the average high-yield savings rate over these 16 years (roughly 1.7%), here's where those accounts would stand:

"The high-yield savings account with $500 in it will be gone after one year. The high-yield savings account with $1,000 in it will last two years," Bodman pointed out.

The $5,000 account would stretch longer but still empty after about 11 years. Only the $10,000 account survives all 16 years — barely.

"It will end with about $3,600 in it," Bodman explained. "You took out $8,000. You have about $3,600 left so the high-yield savings account only earned about $1,600 in interest on your original $10,000 over 16 years."

For most of this 16-year window, high-yield savings accounts were practically useless for earning money .

"The interest rates were near zero from 2010 to 2015 and again in 2020 and 2021," said Bodman, noting that they only started to go up toward 4%after 2022. "So, a high-yield savings account with $10,000 in it earning 1% interest would only earn $100 in interest per year while you were taking out $500."

Put another way: you weren't drawing from the interest. You were draining the principal. At that rate, your withdrawals were always going to outpace your earnings.

This scenario isn't a knock against high-yield savings accounts themselves.

As Bodman explained, "A high-yield savings account is meant to keep your money safe and easy to access, not to help it grow or to provide an income." It's a parking spot for cash you might need, not an investment vehicle.

"If you need an account that will earn interest and last, a high-yield savings account is not the choice especially during years when the interest rate is near zero."

The real lesson? If you're systematically pulling money out of a low-interest account, the math works against you — fast. The solution isn't to find a better savings account; it's to rethink your withdrawal strategy.

articles.title: The Tax Cost of Cashing Out PTO Before Retirement, According to a CPA
articles.summary: Read on to explore the tax cost of cashing out PTO before retirement.
articles.body:
It can be a tempting proposition: Cash out your paid time off (PTO) as you approach retirement. But if you're not careful, that financial move can have unintended consequences that cost you a great deal of money and frustration.

According to Chad Cummings, attorney and certified public accountant (CPA) at Cummings & Cummings Law , a large PTO cash-out can turn an otherwise ordinary retirement year into a tax problem . In fact, he's working on one of these cases right now.

"Here is the correct mindset employees should have: I would treat accrued PTO as deferred wages, not found money," Cummings said. "A $60,000 payout stacks on top of salary, bonus income, investment income and retirement distributions for that calendar year. Remember, that's taxable income, not a tax-free windfall."

Below MoneyLion explores the tax cost of cashing out PTO before retirement, including the impact on your tax bracket, retirement contributions and, ultimately, how much you'll actually be pocketing.

Think About the Impacts of Payroll Withholding

Per Cummings, certified financial planner (CFP), payroll withholding offsets this somewhat but can create a dangerous false sense of security.

"Employers may withhold supplemental wages at a flat federal rate, but that withholding does not cap the employee's actual tax liability," he explained. "Someone already in a higher marginal bracket can owe thousands more at filing, not to mention penalties and interest for underwithholding. Whenever cashing out PTO, the wage earner should sit down with his or her CPA and make a determination if an additional tax payment should be made to the IRS and/or state taxing authorities."

Remember, Cummings noted, PTO generally remains subject to Social Security and Medicare payroll taxes. For someone approaching Medicare, a large income spike can also increase future Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amount (IRMAA) premiums because Medicare looks back two tax years, he added.

"Timing matters, of course," Cummings said. "A retiree who intends to perform Roth conversions, realize capital gains or implement gifting to heirs can lose much of the expected benefit when a six-figure PTO payment unexpectedly increases adjusted gross income."

Jacob Bayer, certified financial planner (CFP) and founder of Jacob Bayer Wealth Management , said to watch the interaction with a retirement-year Roth conversion.

"Clients often plan a conversion for the year they retire," Bayer added. "A PTO payout in that same year eats the bracket space the conversion was going to use. Sequence the two rather than let them collide."

articles.title: Piston raises $15M to expand cardless fuel payments network
articles.summary: Piston has raised $15 million in Series A funding as the cardless fuel payments startup expands its network across the U.S. and adds AI-powered tools for fra...
articles.body:
Piston, a payment platform designed for commercial fleets, has raised $15 million in Series A funding as the company looks to expand its cardless fuel payment network across the U.S., according to Piston.

FPV Ventures led the round, with existing investors Spark Capital and Pear VC also participating. The financing brings Piston's total funding to $22.5 million.

The company said its payment volume increased eightfold over the past year, while its merchant network grew 40 times. Piston now operates at more than 2,000 fuel stations across 48 states and said its point-of-sale integrations are certified and live on systems representing more than 95% of U.S. merchant fuel sites.

Piston's technology is aimed at replacing physical fuel cards with a system that authorizes transactions for individual drivers and vehicles at the point of sale. The company says the approach is intended to give fleets more immediate visibility into fuel spending while reducing the fraud and administrative work associated with physical cards.

"Commercial fuel still runs on payment technology built for another era," said Vikram Sekhon, Piston's co-founder and CEO. "Fleet fuel fraud is a physical card problem, disguised as a detection issue."

The company is also adding AI tools to the platform as it looks to give fleets more control over fuel transactions and the data generated by them, according to Piston.

The first product, called Piston Guard, evaluates each transaction for anomalies and can flag or block suspected fraudulent spending before the transaction is completed, according to the company. A second product, the Piston Analytics Agent, is designed to help fleet operators analyze their spending data and identify patterns without having to manually sort through the information.

The AI products build on Piston's focus on real-time transaction controls, giving fleets tools to identify potentially fraudulent purchases as well as analyze spending after transactions occur.

Piston was founded by Sekhon and co-founder Shivam Shah, who previously operated trucking fleets. Sekhon previously told FreightWaves that he operated between 120 and 250 trucks and that fuel was his fleet's second-largest expense after payroll. He said the fleet had dealt with fraud, unpredictable fees and the administrative work involved in reconciling fuel transactions.

That experience helped shape Piston's approach to fuel payments. In 2025, the company said drivers used a smartphone and a dynamic QR code to authorize fuel purchases, with transactions tied to details including the vehicle, time, location and fuel type.

articles.title: BC aperta regras para criptoativos e exige aviso ao Coaf para transferências acima de US$ 10 mil | G1
articles.standfirst: Exigência vale para operações com origem ou destino em carteiras autocustodiadas e entra em vigor em 1º de outubro.
articles.summary: Exigência vale para operações com origem ou destino em carteiras autocustodiadas e entra em vigor em 1º de outubro.
articles.body:
O Banco Central do Brasil (BC) anunciou nesta quarta-feira (23) ajustes nas regras para o mercado de ativos virtuais , como as criptomoedas, e nas normas de prevenção à lavagem de dinheiro e ao financiamento do terrorismo relacionadas a esses ativos.

Uma das principais mudanças determina que transferências de criptoativos de valor igual ou superior ao equivalente a US$ 10 mil , realizadas para ou a partir de carteiras autocustodiadas, passem a ser comunicadas ao Conselho de Controle de Atividades Financeiras (Coaf).

🔎 Carteiras autocustodiadas são aquelas em que o próprio usuário mantém o controle das chaves privadas que permitem movimentar seus criptoativos, sem depender de uma instituição ou plataforma para guardá-los.

Segundo o BC, a medida busca ampliar a capacidade de monitoramento dessas operações , já que esse tipo de carteira pode oferecer menos informações para avaliação de riscos do que ativos mantidos sob custódia de instituições autorizadas.

A instituição acrescentou que as alterações têm o objetivo de "fortalecer a segurança e a integridade do mercado de ativos virtuais", além de dar mais previsibilidade aos participantes do setor e facilitar o processamento das informações necessárias à supervisão.

Outra mudança nas regras de prevenção à lavagem de dinheiro determina a comunicação automática ao Coaf de operações de câmbio com entrega ou recebimento de moeda estrangeira em dinheiro vivo de valor igual ou superior a US$ 10 mil.

Segundo a instituição, a medida busca promover um "tratamento regulatório mais uniforme para operações realizadas com recursos em espécie".

As novas regras entram em vigor em 1º de outubro de 2026.

O mês também marca o prazo final para que as sociedades prestadoras de ativos virtuais (PSAVs) já em operação formalizem seus pedidos de autorização junto ao BC.

articles.title: EUA e China prorrogam trégua comercial até janeiro, diz secretário do Tesouro americano | G1
articles.standfirst: Anúncio ocorre um dia antes da cúpula entre Donald Trump e o presidente da China, Xi Jinping, marcada para esta quinta-feira (24), em território americano.
articles.summary: Anúncio ocorre um dia antes da cúpula entre Donald Trump e o presidente da China, Xi Jinping, marcada para esta quinta-feira (24), em território americano.
articles.body:
O secretário de Tesouro dos Estados Unidos, Scott Bessent, durante anúncio de novo pacote de snações ao Irã, em 24 de agosto de 2026. — Foto: Evelyn Hockstein/ Reuters

O secretário do Tesouro americano, Scott Bessent, afirmou nesta quarta-feira (23) que os Estados Unidos e a China concordaram em estender por dois meses a trégua comercial que expiraria em 10 de novembro. Com isso, o acordo permanece em vigor até janeiro.

Segundo Bessent, a medida dará mais tempo para que os dois países negociem um acordo potencialmente mais amplo. A declaração foi feita à Fox News horas após sua segunda reunião, em quatro dias, com o vice-primeiro-ministro chinês, He Lifeng.

Os encontros serviram para preparar a cúpula entre o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump , e o presidente da China, Xi Jinping, marcada para esta quinta-feira (24). Xi desembarcou nos EUA nesta quarta-feira.

“Nos reunimos hoje para ver se conseguiríamos fazer um acordo maior, em vez de apenas uma série de medidas menores”, disse o chefe do Tesouro.

Segundo ele, a extensão de dois meses da trégua comercial, acordada em maio em Busan, na Coreia do Sul, dará aos dois países “mais tempo para ver o que podemos fazer na área econômica”.

Mais cedo, Bessent disse a jornalistas que Pequim levantou a possibilidade de um acordo comercial mais amplo entre EUA e China durante 12 horas de negociações realizadas no domingo , mas não deu detalhes sobre o alcance desse eventual pacto. Segundo o Tesouro americano, a reunião desta quarta-feira durou cerca de 90 minutos.

Questionado sobre a possibilidade de um acordo ser fechado até 10 de janeiro, Bessent respondeu à Fox News que isso ainda não está claro. Ele acrescentou que Washington também pressiona a China para que cumpra de forma mais ampla os compromissos assumidos no acordo atual nos próximos meses.

Segundo ele, Pequim está cumprindo a exigência de comprar 25 milhões de toneladas de soja, mas ainda está abaixo da meta de adquirir US$ 17 bilhões em outros produtos agrícolas.

Autoridades americanas disseram na semana passada que as entregas chinesas de terras raras também estão abaixo do esperado.

A cúpula de quinta-feira, a segunda de até quatro encontros previstos entre Trump e Xi neste ano, poderá trazer anúncios sobre a meta dos dois países de eliminar tarifas sobre US$ 30 bilhões em produtos não essenciais , além de temas relacionados a serviços financeiros e compras agrícolas, afirmou Bessent.

“Considerando que este pode ser um ano histórico, em que os líderes podem se reunir até quatro vezes, sendo este o segundo encontro, com reuniões previstas também em Shenzhen e Miami, estamos abertos tanto à ideia de manter o arranjo de Busan quanto à de avaliar um acordo mais amplo”, disse Bessent mais cedo a jornalistas.

“Estamos confortáveis com as duas opções e vamos fazer o que for melhor para o povo americano”, acrescentou.

Em publicação na rede X, Bessent classificou as discussões como substanciais e afirmou que o Tesouro está focado em garantir compromissos que protejam trabalhadores, agricultores e empresas americanas, ao mesmo tempo em que promovam os interesses econômicos e de segurança nacional do país.

Bessent afirmou ter se reunido com He na sede do Banco Mundial, em Washington, para resolver algumas “questões pendentes” antes da cúpula entre Trump e Xi. Segundo ele, o governo Trump busca uma relação estratégica baseada em “reciprocidade e justiça”.

Bessent, He e o representante de Comércio dos EUA, Jamieson Greer, se reuniram em Nova York no domingo para preparar possíveis acordos sobre comércio e inteligência artificial que poderão ser analisados pelos dois líderes.

O secretário do Tesouro americano classificou as negociações como bem-sucedidas e afirmou que os dois países concordaram em criar uma “linha direta” de comunicação para informar um ao outro sobre incidentes de segurança envolvendo inteligência artificial.

A resposta da China ao plano da linha direta de IA não ficou clara . A agência estatal chinesa Xinhua apenas reconheceu que os dois países discutiram inteligência artificial.

Analistas das relações entre EUA e China afirmam que as expectativas de cooperação em IA são baixas devido à falta de confiança mútua e ao fato de que nenhum dos dois países demonstrou interesse significativo em desacelerar o desenvolvimento da tecnologia.

Trump, inclusive, tem dito o contrário: que não pretende “frear” o crescimento da IA e que manterá a liderança dos EUA sobre a China no que agora chama de “superinteligência”.

A chamada “distensão econômica” de Busan reduziu drasticamente as tarifas bilaterais, que haviam alcançado percentuais de três dígitos após uma escalada de retaliações mútuas desencadeada pelos aumentos tarifários promovidos por Trump no ano passado.

A China também concordou em restabelecer o fluxo de ímãs de terras raras e de outros minerais críticos, cujas exportações havia restringido severamente.

articles.title: People Are Moving Less Than Ever—and It’s Costing Them Career and Lifestyle Upgrades
articles.summary: Americans, especially millennials, are shunning moves of all kinds with increasing frequency this year, a new study finds.
articles.body:
When Rebecca Obeng began hunting for a new job after finishing medical training in Chicago , she didn't expect to end up in Cleveland .

Obeng, who's originally from Ghana, went to medical school in Virginia and then a residency in Georgia. But the Midwest struck her as a place to stay. The University Hospitals pathologist ended up buying a home in Mayfield, OH , after finding many more affordable options than the Windy City held.

"The job was the type of structure I was looking for, but beyond that, I really liked Cleveland when I visited. I was quite surprised," Obeng tells Realtor.com® . "It's just very green. Not too overwhelming. And feels like it has this rich history and tradition."

"And my rent in Chicago was pretty much what I'm paying for my mortgage now," Obeng continues. "It ended up being a much better value in terms of housing."

Moving for work is ubiquitous in America, and so is trading the big city for a more affordable life elsewhere. But a recent analysis by Bank of America found that Americans, especially millennials, are shunning moves of all kinds with increasing frequency. And that has implications for an already challenged housing market.

According to recent U.S. Census Bureau data, the nation's residential mobility rate has fallen to a historic low of roughly 11%, down from the 20% annual mover rate recorded during the mid-20th century. This represents the lowest level of geographic movement recorded since federal tracking began in 1948.

Bank of America's data found a broad-based slowdown in moving. That includes both long-distance moves and moves within cities. Millennials in particular see the sharpest pullbacks. But aside from Gen Z, all age groups are increasingly staying put, the data found.

Relocations typically show a rise in the spring and a trough late in the year, matching the seasonal housing market cycle. But the historical shape of the data has been replaced by a sharp drop that has mostly persisted since late 2025, Bank of America found.

"Americans are moving less, and the slowdown is broad-based," wrote Joe Wadford , an economist at the Bank of America Institute. But lower-income households and millennials are seeing the sharpest pullbacks.

"When people do change locales, they still favor smaller cities, especially those in the Midwest," Wadford said.

Meanwhile, those who would typically move to new homes in the same city seem to be favoring renovating their properties instead of moving, Bank of America said.

articles.title: A new measure of financial conditions shows the US economy heading for a rough patch
articles.summary: Jim Paulsen unveiled a gauge to measure the relative tightness of financial conditions. He says the indicators point to a period of economic weakness.
articles.body:
Market vet Jim Paulsen is warning of more weakness for the US economy ahead.

The longtime strategist unveiled a new gauge that tracks the tightness of financial conditions.

The gauge is currently in a territory that has preceded every major recession since 1970, he said.

The US economy looks like it's headed for a spell of weakness, a veteran strategist is warning.

Jim Paulsen, a Wall Street economist and the former chief investment strategist at the Leuthold Group, sees a troubling trajectory ahead for the US, with the economy likely to see weak growth going forward, pressured by a "cocktail of past contractionary forces" acting on the economy, he wrote on his Substack this week.

Paulsen said he created a new gauge to measure tightness of financial conditions, pointing to how accommodative or restrictive the broader macro backdrop is for growth. The Leading Financial Conditions Gauge measures five economic policies and three economic forces. It has proven to be a leading indicator of economic growth and stock prices, Paulsen said, citing his analysis of the gauge's swings dating back to 1970.

Of the eight indicators in the model, seven represent a contractionary force on the economy, Paulsen said. Here's the rundown of the gauge's contractionary signals:

Long-term and short-term yields are rising. The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield hit a new post-Financial Crisis peak this week, rising as high as 5.09%. The 2-year Treasury yield, meanwhile, rose to 4.89%, its highest level in about two years as investors fretted about the outlook for inflation and US fiscal health.

The yield curve has flattened, which indicates that short-term yields are rising faster relative to long-term yields. That points to market expectations for higher short-term rates, which can slow the economy.

Fiscal support could be fading. The US's net deficit spending is falling, a sign that the economy isn't getting as much fiscal stimulus as it used to. The federal budget deficit clocked in at $2 trillion in the first 11 months of the 2026 fiscal year, $6 billion less compared to the same period last year, according to estimates from the Congressional Budget Office .

Oil prices are higher. Brent crude , the international benchmark, traded around $101 a barrel on Wednesday, sitting above the critical $100-a-barrel mark.

Inflation is rising. The consumer price index held steady in August, but there are other indicators that suggest inflation is accelerating. Core CPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, rose 0.3% last month, above last month's 0.2% gain.

Real wages are falling. After accounting for inflation, average hourly earnings for all workers fell 0.1% in August, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

articles.title: We don't want to compete with customers, may not run airline: Adani Airports CEO
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Adani Airports CEO Arun Bansal said the company does not want to compete with its airline customers and has enough opportunities in the airport
articles.body: MUMBAI: Adani Airports CEO Arun Bansal said the company does not want to compete with its airline customers and has enough opportunities in the airport business, a day after govt said it was examining the pros and cons of allowing airport operators such as Adani Group to run airlines."As airport CEO, I would not like to compete with my own customers. My hands are full," Bansal said at SBI Banking and Economics Conclave. Bansal said the growth opportunity in India's aviation sector was large enough for Adani Airports to focus its bandwidth on expanding its airport operations rather than entering the airline business."India will be the fastest-growing aviation market in the world over the next 10 years and will be among the top two markets," he said. Adani Airports currently handles about 100 million passengers and Bansal said the company expected India's aviation sector to grow substantially over the next two decades. With GDP potentially growing eightfold in 20 years and aviation growing faster than GDP, the sector could expand about tenfold, he said. "If we are able to capture that, we will be number one in the world," Bansal said.Adani Airports is already the second-largest airport operator globally by passenger traffic, according to Bansal. The company operates airports including Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Lucknow, Thiruvananthapuram, Jaipur, Guwahati and Navi Mumbai.Bansal said the company planned to invest about $11 billion in airport infrastructure in India over the next five years.You use AI every day. articles.title: Meta unveils $1,299 VR Glasses, camera-less smart glasses at Meta Connect
articles.body:
Meta ( META ) launched three new pairs of smart glasses during the company's Meta Connect conference on Wednesday.

CEO Mark Zuckerberg took the stage to show off the trio of devices, which includes the company's first Meta VR Glasses, the camera-free Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses, and the third generation of its Ray-Ban Meta glasses.

The $1,299 Meta VR Glasses are the standout of the trio, offering virtual reality capabilities in a glasses-style design, which makes other VR headsets look ancient by comparison.

On sale in spring 2027, the company says the high-tech eyewear is five times lighter than its Meta Quest 3 headset, and features a 5K display for watching shows and 3D movies, playing games, and working.

Because you're looking at two screens, there are external cameras so that you can see the world around you while wearing them.

The glass's computing components, battery, and storage are housed in a separate dedicated puck that tethers to the spectacles, helping to ensure they're light enough to wear for long periods.

To navigate, you use hand gestures or can speak to the on-board Muse AI agent. And unlike in the Muse app, you'll see a fully rendered version of your custom Muse avatar.

For film buffs, Meta says the VR Glasses are the first-ever IMAX Enhanced-certified VR device, allowing customers to watch IMAX movies at home.

The company is also partnering with Disney+ ( DIS ) to give users access to movies like "The Avengers" and "Black Panther." Meta says it's working to bring Amazon's ( AMZN ) Prime Video, Google's ( GOOG , GOOGL ) YouTube, and other streamers to the platform, as well.

In the office, the Meta VR Glasses can display a single large virtual display or several smaller ones, allowing you to switch between apps throughout the day. Flat surfaces turn into virtual keyboards and mice, letting you navigate and type documents without the need for secondary accessories.

For gamers, Microsoft ( MSFT ) is bringing its Xbox Cloud Gaming service to the glasses, so users can play on the go.

Meta is also introducing what it calls its hologram calling technology. Users take a picture of themselves in the Meta AI app, which then creates a full-body digital version of them that they can use to make video calls with friends and family while wearing the glasses. Apple has a similar feature for its Vision Pro headset.

In addition to the Meta VR Glasses, Meta also unveiled the company's $349 Ray-Ban Meta Audio smart glasses.

Unlike the standard Ray-Ban Meta glasses, the Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses come sans cameras, making them look far more like a standard pair of Ray-Bans.

articles.title: Gold Holds Drop as Higher Oil and Hot US Data Fan Rate-Hike Bets
articles.summary: Gold held a decline as resurgent energy prices and stronger-than-expected US economic data increased bets the Federal Reserve might again raise interest rate...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Gold held a decline as resurgent energy prices and stronger-than-expected US economic data increased bets the Federal Reserve might again raise interest rates to combat inflation.

Bullion was trading around $4,290 an ounce, after falling 1.7% the day before. Oil rose after a defiant Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told the United Nations his country won't allow freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz while sanctions and a US blockade remain in place, underscoring the difficulty in reaching a peace deal with Washington despite efforts to revive talks this week.

He added that Iran is ready to negotiate but will not respond to threats, and while it isn't interested in building an atomic weapon, it won't give up the right to develop nuclear technology for economic reasons. This comes a day after President Donald Trump said his officials had "very good" talks with Iranian envoys on the sidelines of the UN summit.

Gold has been dictated by the Fed's rate outlook in recent weeks as investors gauge whether surging energy prices will keep inflationary pressure strong enough to prompt further increases in rates, which would likely be negative for bullion as it pays no interest. It's down around a fifth since the US-Iran war erupted in late February.

Losses in the US Treasuries market intensified on stronger-than-forecast economic data and a weak debt auction, reflecting the view that inflation is likely to remain sticky. Treasury yields across most maturities hit the highest in almost two decades, while five-year US yields moved above 5% for the first time since 2007.

US business activity rose at the fastest pace in more than five years as robust demand pushed up new orders and employment at manufacturers and service providers. The S&P Global flash US composite purchasing managers index climbed to 58.4 in September, the highest since July 2021.

Fed Governor Michael Barr said further rate increases are likely needed to return inflation to the central bank's 2% target. His comments follow a string of similar warnings from fellow policymakers in recent days that price pressures appear to be persistent. Swap markets are currently pricing in at least three hikes by April next year, an increase from earlier this week.

articles.title: NSE IPO: Stock lists at Rs 1,800 versus issue price of Rs 1,785 on BSE with 0.8% premium; check details
articles.summary: NSE IPO listing date today: National Stock Exchange of India’s shares debuted on the Bombay Stock Exchange at Rs 1,800 versus an issue price of Rs 1,785,
articles.body: NSE IPO listing date today: National Stock Exchange of India’s shares debuted on the Bombay Stock Exchange at Rs 1,800 versus an issue price of Rs 1,785, marking a premium of around 0.8%.NSE made its stock market debut with a market capitalisation of more than Rs 4.45 lakh crore, becoming the second listed stock exchange in India. Its valuation at listing was significantly higher than that of rival BSE, whose current market capitalisation stands at Rs 1.33 lakh crore.Market participants were tracking grey market movements closely ahead of the listing, which is among the most anticipated market debuts of the year so far. Analysts said restrictions on exits by most large shareholders could limit the availability of NSE shares in the near term, potentially putting upward pressure on prices at a later stage.NSE's market debut gives investors an opportunity to assess how the exchange should be valued. Its longer-term growth outlook helped attract strong institutional interest, while retail investors appeared more cautious amid concerns about derivatives volumes, regulatory pressures and the possibility of more shares entering the market.Although investors remain broadly positive on NSE's longer-term prospects, the stock's performance in the months following its listing could depend on the amount of additional equity that becomes available once the lock-in periods for existing shareholders come to an end.NSE Debuts on BSE, MSEIIn a circular issued on Wednesday, MSE said NSE's equity shares would be admitted for trading on its capital market segment under the ‘Permitted to trade’ category, effective September 24.The Metropolitan Stock Exchange is a Sebi-recognised national stock exchange that operates an electronic trading platform covering capital markets, equity derivatives, currency derivatives and debt segments. Its platform includes equity and index derivatives, debt and currency derivatives, with more than 250 listings and over 3,100 companies available for trading.The development comes days after NSE MD and CEO Ashish Chauhan made it clear that the exchange would not approach Sebi for permission to trade its own shares on its platform. Existing regulations of the market regulator do not permit a recognised stock exchange to list its own securities on its own trading platform.NSE IPO GMPIn the unlisted market, traders saw a grey market premium or GMP of around 2.2%. The stock has listed on a waek note with less than 1% premium over its issue price.The GMP was much higher earlier at Rs 250-310 a share, or roughly 14-17%. The steep decline had suggested expectations of only modest gains when the shares list."While investors have been waiting for the NSE listing for long, the enthusiasm has moderated because of the large issue size and expected supply," Abhay Doshi, co-founder of UnlistedArena.com told ET.At the IPO's upper price of Rs 1,785 per share, NSE's valuation stands at Rs 4.42 lakh crore, compared with Rs 1.33 lakh crore for rival BSE. Some market participants said the balance between available supply and investor demand could play an important role in determining how NSE shares perform in the initial trading sessions after listing.The listing brings to an end NSE's long-running journey towards becoming a listed company and make it India's second listed stock exchange after BSE.NSE launched its initial public offering earlier this month, seeking to raise Rs 22,562 crore through a 12.64 crore-share offer for sale (OFS) by existing shareholders.Since the issue was entirely an OFS, NSE itself will not receive any money from the IPO. The proceeds will instead accrue to the shareholders selling their stakes through the offering.The IPO price band was fixed at Rs 1,700 to Rs 1,785 per share. With the lot size set at 8 shares, retail investors were required to invest a minimum of Rs 14,280 to apply for the issue.Before the IPO opened for subscription, NSE had raised Rs 6,746 crore from more than 150 anchor investors.Foreign portfolio investors made up Rs 2,883 crore, or 43%, of the total anchor book. The anchor round saw participation from more than 20 foreign long-only funds, including Singapore sovereign wealth fund GIC, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and Norges Bank.Domestic institutional participation was similarly spread across investors. More than 25 mutual funds, along with 11 insurance and pension companies, invested around Rs 3,588 crore, accounting for 53% of the anchor book.LIC, which is NSE's largest shareholder with a 10.72% stake, also participated in the anchor round. LIC, LIC Mutual Fund and LIC Pension Fund together invested more than Rs 500 crore. The investment was made even though LIC's existing shareholding in NSE is larger than the stake being offered through the IPO.The SBI group also took part in the anchor book through SBI Mutual Fund, SBI General, SBI Life and SBI Pension Fund. State Bank of India and SBI Capital Markets are together selling a 1% stake in NSE, while the group's combined investment in the exchange through its various entities exceeds Rs 400 crore.NSE's first public issue attracted strong demand during the three-day subscription period from September 17 to September 21. The IPO was subscribed nearly six times the shares on offer. Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) drove the demand, subscribing to their reserved portion around 13 times, while the portions allocated to retail investors and non-institutional investors (NII) were subscribed 1.4 times and 6.6 times, respectively.You use AI every day. articles.title: Tokyo Used Condo Prices Drop for First Time in Over Two Years
articles.summary: Used condominium prices in Tokyo dropped for the first time in more than two years in August as rising mortgage rates start to weigh on sentiment among home...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Used condominium prices in Tokyo dropped for the first time in more than two years in August as rising mortgage rates start to weigh on sentiment among home buyers, according to a research firm.

The average price of condos in Japan's capital dropped 0.2% from the previous month to ¥112.74 million ($714,000), marking the first decline in 28 months, Tokyo Kantei Co. wrote in a report released Thursday. Prices began falling in previous months in the more expensive city center areas, suggesting that weakness in the city's condominium market is spreading.

Mortgage costs are climbing in Japan as the central bank raises interest rates and signals its willingness to tighten credit further, damping condo demand from home buyers. Japan's Financial Services Agency has said it will strengthen its oversight of real estate lending amid concern that property prices are overshooting in Tokyo, driven by domestic and international investors rushing in, chasing capital gains.

"Price adjustments for properties in central Tokyo are expected to continue toward the end of the year," said Masayuki Takahashi, senior principal researcher at Tokyo Kantei. "Similar movements will continue not only in central Tokyo but also in surrounding areas."

Highlighting the earlier condo price declines in the more expensive areas of the metropolis, the average price of properties in Tokyo's six central wards fell 0.7% from the previous month, marking the fourth consecutive month of declines. The prices are adjusted to represent 70 square meter units.
